Hi Nina / Ken —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align internal stakeholders on the Acrosoft pilot (search & summarization use case):

- Business goal: pilot 2-week POC to validate latency/cost and integration surface.
- Decision criteria: latency SLA < 300ms median for 1k qps, embed similarity >= 0.92 for our evals, predictable per-token pricing.
- Suggested sequence: NDA (if needed) → pilot kickoff → MSA for pilot terms → DPA prior to production.

Could you confirm: 1) who owns NDA review at Acrosoft (legal)? 2) who owns MSA & procurement (economic contact)? 3) typical legal/procurement turn times and any redline sequencing preferences?

I'm looping in David (solutions) and Laura (sales ops) to help with mutual action plan and any procurement intake forms.

Proposed next steps:
- We can attach a short mutual action plan and an initial NDA draft for your legal review.
- If procurement wants a single-chart of steps/owners, Laura can prepare it today.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for the clear sequence. Quick answers from our side:

- NDA & legal review: Legal intake goes to legal@acrosoft.com (I will also escalate to our legal lead, Priya Rao). Priya generally does a quick review for mutual NDAs within 2-4 business days if no substantive redlines.
- MSA & procurement owner: Procurement (procurement@acrosoft.com) owns the MSA; Ken (cc'd) will be our primary procurement contact for commercial terms. Typical MSA negotiation for a new vendor runs 3-4 weeks depending on redlines.
- DPA/security: Security & privacy review comes after commercial terms; our security team usually wants the latest DPA and a short answers-first questionnaire. Security turn time is ~5-7 business days for a standard vendor, longer if we need evidence.

For sequencing we prefer: NDA (if required) → brief pilot SOW addendum to MSA → MSA redlines and commercial terms → DPA & security questionnaire. If Redwood can accept an Acrosoft standard MSA with limited redlines, that speeds things up.

I'll send the legal intake contact (Priya) and procurement intake form to you separately.

—Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Product Partnerships, Acrosoft

Quick internal note and operational ask —

Thanks Marissa. I'll prepare a one-page mutual action plan and a sequencing chart for procurement/legal. Suggested sequencing based on Acrosoft's timeline:

1) NDA (2-4 business days) — initial quick mutual NDA; keep it mutual and narrow scope to pilot.
2) Pilot SOW (attached to MSA) — one-page SOW that defines scope, duration, basic success metrics.
3) MSA negotiation (2-4 weeks) — commercial terms, indemnity/limits, liability. Redline sequencing: prioritize commercial terms first; legal redlines around IP and liability can be tabled until after commercial alignment to avoid blocking.
4) DPA / Security questionnaire (1-2 weeks after MSA agreement) — ready to share Redwood's standard DPA + an abbreviated Security Q&A. If Acrosoft requires SOC 2 or pen-test evidence, note that could add time.

I'll upload the one-pager and an editable NDA draft to the shared Doc and send the link here shortly.

—Laura
